title: Detect data drift and accuracy decay
instructions:
## The model did not change; the world did

A credit-scoring model was trained on last year's applicants. Two monitors are standard.

1. `psi(expected, actual)`: the Population Stability Index between two histograms of counts over the same bins: convert each to proportions, replace zeros with 0.0001, and sum `(a − e) · ln(a / e)` over bins. Values above 0.2 indicate significant drift.
2. `drift_level(value)`: `"stable"` below 0.1, `"moderate"` from 0.1 to below 0.2, `"significant"` from 0.2.
3. `rolling_accuracy(y_true, y_pred, window)`: a list with the accuracy of each consecutive window of that size (non-overlapping, drop an incomplete tail).
hints: Proportions: e = [c / sum(expected) for c in expected]; same for actual; then max(p, 0.0001) for each.
psi = sum((a - e) * math.log(a / e) for e, a in zip(exp_p, act_p)).
for start in range(0, len(y_true) - window + 1, window): slice both lists and compute the share of equal pairs.
realityNote: Evidently, Arize and the cloud ML monitors compute PSI and KS statistics per feature on a schedule and alert when a threshold is crossed; the hard part in practice is getting the true labels late enough to measure accuracy at all.
